framework: CEFR (Common European Framework of Reference for Languages)

A1_A2_Elementary.title: Present simple: be and other verbs
A1_A2_Elementary.description: Using 'to be' (am/is/are) and action verbs to talk about routine, states and facts.
key_examples: I am a student.
She works in a hospital.
They do not live in London.

A1_A2_Elementary.title: Possessives and Demonstratives
A1_A2_Elementary.description: Possessive adjectives (my, your, his, her, its, our, their) and demonstratives (this, that, these, those).
key_examples: This is my coat.
Those shoes are very comfortable.

exercises.q: Look at ___ bird over there in the tree!
exercises.explanation: That refers to a singular object at a distance.

A1_A2_Elementary.title: Past simple: regular and irregular verbs
A1_A2_Elementary.description: Forming past simple sentences with -ed and common irregular verbs (went, bought, saw, did).
key_examples: We watched a movie yesterday.
He bought a new laptop last week.

exercises.explanation: Past simple irregular form of 'go' is 'went'.

A1_A2_Elementary.title: Comparatives and Superlatives
A1_A2_Elementary.description: Comparing people, items and qualities with -er/-est and more/most.
A1_A2_Elementary.formula: Adj-er than / More + Adj than / The most + Adj
key_examples: Tokyo is bigger than Rome.
The blue whale is the largest animal.

exercises.q: This test is ___ (difficult) than the previous one.

B1_B2_Intermediate.title: Present perfect with for and since
B1_B2_Intermediate.description: Connecting past actions to the present, indicating duration (for) or starting point (since).
key_examples: I have lived here for five years.
She has known him since 2018.

exercises.explanation: Since is used with specific starting point in time.

B1_B2_Intermediate.title: Conditionals: First and Second Conditionals
B1_B2_Intermediate.description: Real future possibilities vs hypothetical/imaginary situations.
B1_B2_Intermediate.formula: 1st: If + present, will + V_inf | 2nd: If + past, would + V_inf
key_examples: If it rains, we will stay at home.
If I won the lottery, I would travel the world.

exercises.q: If I ___ you, I would take that job offer.
exercises.explanation: In 2nd conditional, 'were' is standard with all subjects.

B1_B2_Intermediate.title: Passive Voice in Academic Contexts
B1_B2_Intermediate.description: Shifting focus to the action or receiver; essential for IELTS Academic Task 1 & Task 2.
B1_B2_Intermediate.formula: S + be + past participle (+ by Agent)
key_examples: The data was gathered over a five-month period.
New safety protocols are being implemented.

exercises.explanation: Future simple passive: will be + V3.

B1_B2_Intermediate.title: Modal verbs of deduction and speculation
B1_B2_Intermediate.description: Must, can't, might, could to express degree of certainty in present and past.
B1_B2_Intermediate.formula: Modal + be / Modal + have + past participle
key_examples: She can't be at home; her car isn't outside.
They must have missed the morning train.

exercises.q: He's not answering his phone. He ___ (must / can't) be sleeping.

C1_Advanced.title: Inversion for Emphasis
C1_Advanced.description: Inverting subject and auxiliary verb after negative or restrictive adverbs.
key_examples: Rarely have I witnessed such dedication.
No sooner had we arrived than it started to pour.

exercises.q: Seldom ___ such remarkable talent in an audition.
exercises.explanation: Inversion requires auxiliary before subject after 'seldom'.

C1_Advanced.title: Mixed Conditionals and Subjunctive Structures
C1_Advanced.description: Combining past condition with present result, or unreal present condition with past result.
C1_Advanced.formula: If + past perfect, would + V_inf (Past cause -> Present effect)
key_examples: If I had taken that plane, I would be in Sydney now.
I demand that he be present at the hearing.

exercises.q: If she had accepted the promotion last year, she ___ a director now.
exercises.explanation: Past condition leading to present result.
